title: Every Sky Primitive Instance is wrapped in an identical Hub Document lifecycle, so status is readable without knowing the Primitive
content:
Across A.6.1.1.3.2.1 and A.6.1.1.3.2.2, each Primitive Keel uses is represented by the same fixed skeleton: a Primitive Hub Document that "organizes all base information relevant to Keel's usage" of it, a Global Activation Status (`Completed`, `Active`, or `Inactive`), Directories for Active / Completed / In Progress Instances, and a Hub Data Repository.

The Instance level repeats a second fixed skeleton: Parameters (including a Custom Instance Parameters slot "if any"), an Operational Process Definition, and a Data Repository holding Initial Planning, Operational GovOps Review, and Artifact Edit Proposal materials.

The payoff is that an Agent's operational state can be read positionally. To learn whether Keel's Executor Transformation has ever run, a reader checks one address (A.6.1.1.3.2.1.3.1.1 — `Inactive`) without understanding what the Primitive does. The same query works for every Primitive and every Agent, because the skeleton is invariant.

The cost is bulk: the great majority of Core units in a Prime Agent Artifact are empty structural slots, and a reader must distinguish "present but empty" from "substantively defined." The Atlas accepts that verbosity in exchange for uniform machine- and human-navigable state, and in exchange for the fact that every Primitive already has a place to put its evidence trail before that evidence exists.
description: One Global Activation Status plus Active / Completed / In Progress directories and a Data Repository repeat for every Primitive, making Agent state auditable by position rather than by content.
